question: In which year did plague strike Bombay?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1896**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The plague struck Bombay in the year **1896**.
 
• This outbreak was part of the Third Pandemic, which started in China and spread to other parts of the world, including India.
 
• The plague in Bombay led to significant social and economic disruption, affecting a large portion of the population.
 
• Efforts to control the plague included quarantine measures, sanitation improvements, and the evacuation of affected areas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Plague**

 
 
• The plague is a serious infectious disease caused by the bacterium *Yersinia pestis*.
 
• There are three main forms of plague: bubonic, septicemic, and pneumonic. The bubonic form is the most common.
 
• Historically, plague outbreaks have caused widespread pandemics, such as the Black Death in the 14th century.
 
 
 
• **Third Pandemic**
 
 
• The Third Pandemic of plague began in the Yunnan province of China in the 1850s.
 
• It spread to port cities around the world through shipping routes, reaching India in the late 19th century.
 
• The Third Pandemic caused millions of deaths worldwide and continued to be a significant health threat until the mid-20th century.
 
 
 
• **Sanitation and Quarantine Measures**
 
 
• Sanitation improvements included measures like cleaning streets, removing waste, and improving water supply systems to prevent the spread of the disease.
 
• Quarantine measures involved isolating affected individuals and communities to stop the transmission of the plague.
 
• These measures were crucial in controlling the spread of infectious diseases during outbreaks.
